angularDiameterSource: Vega is a rapid rotator seen nearly pole-on: Monnier et al. (2012), ApJ 761, L3, measure an equatorial radius of 2.726 ± 0.006 and a polar radius of 2.418 ± 0.012 solar radii with CHARA/MIRC. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of those two, 2.62 solar radii; the flattening is not drawn.
distanceSource: Inverse of the Hipparcos new-reduction parallax 130.23 ± 0.36 mas (van Leeuwen 2007) via SIMBAD
radiusSource: Radius: Vega is a rapid rotator seen nearly pole-on: Monnier et al. (2012), ApJ 761, L3, measure an equatorial radius of 2.726 ± 0.006 and a polar radius of 2.418 ± 0.012 solar radii with CHARA/MIRC. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of those two, 2.62 solar radii; the flattening is not drawn. Adopted 1,822,180 km, 2.6192 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius. No gravitational parameter is adopted. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; no spin axis is adopted.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 9360 ± 90 K, the surface-averaged value of the concordance model in Monnier et al. 2012 (ApJL 761, L3; https://doi.org/10.1088/2041-8205/761/1/L3), Table 2, the same model as the radius. The star is gravity-darkened: the same table gives 10070 K at the pole and 8910 K at the equator.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; no picture of the photosphere is cast.
